topic.title: CSS Themes and Styling
topic.shortdesc: How to use built-in themes, customize CSS variables, and apply platform-specific stylesheets.

body.p: The CSS themesDITA2ePub plugin includes a layered CSS architecture designed for flexibility without complexity. Instead of a single monolithic stylesheet, the plugin uses a cascade of purpose-specific CSS files that are loaded in a defined order. This allows you to change the visual appearance of your EPUB without touching the transformation code.

ol.li: epub-default.css — base styles that define the structural layout, element spacing, and typographic defaults for all EPUBs
epub-theme-{name}.css — theme overrides that adjust colors, fonts, and decorative elements for a specific genre or use case
epub-platform-{name}.css — platform-specific tweaks for reading system quirks (e.g., Kindle rendering differences)
epub-fonts.css — auto-generated @font-face declarations when fonts are embedded
epub-fxl.css — fixed-layout viewport styles (only when epub.layout=fixed)
Custom CSS — your own stylesheet appended last, with highest specificity

body.p: This layering means you can switch from a technical documentation theme to a fiction theme by changing a single parameter, and all structural styles remain intact.
body.note: All themes use CSS custom propertiesCSS custom properties (variables) for colors, spacing, and typography. You can override any variable in a custom CSS file without duplicating entire rule sets.
